@@ -149,6 +149,9 @@
-    while i:

+    i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+    rem3, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+    parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+              pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],

+    parts.reverse()

actions.reason: In b58encode, after the four-groups-per-pass loop, i < base**12, so at most three base**4 groups remain. The trailing `while i:` loop (one divmod, two lookups and a loop test per group) is replaced by straight-line code: when i >= base**4, two divmods give all three remaining groups at once; otherwise a single group is taken directly from i. Any zero digits at the top are removed by the existing lstrip, as before. Outputs are byte-identical (equivalence harness identical). Measured encode_ir ratio 0.9877; decode_ir 0.9967 and check_ir 1.0001 stay within their limits.

diff --git a/base58/__init__.py b/base58/__init__.py
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -146,11 +146,17 @@ def b58encode(
                   pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
                   pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
                   pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq])
-    while i:
-        # Remaining groups one at a time; zero digits at the top of the
-        # last group are removed by the lstrip below
+    if i >= big:
+        # Now base**4 <= i < base**12: two or three groups remain, take
+        # them without a loop. Zero digits at the top of the last group
+        # are removed by the lstrip below.
         i, rem = divmod(i, big)
-        parts += pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq]
+        rem3, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq])
+    elif i:
+        parts += pairs[i % sq], pairs[i // sq]
     parts.reverse()
     return zero * (origlen - newlen) + b''.join(parts).lstrip(zero)

journal.text:
Test agent here. I worked on b58encode in base58/__init__.py, lines 149 onward. After the four-groups-per-pass loop, i is below base**12. So at most three base**4 groups remain. I replaced the trailing while loop with straight-line code. Two divmods give all three groups, or one group is taken directly. Same bytes out is the bar.

First try: identical outputs, encode_ir ratio 0.9853. But check_ir worsened +1.54% against a 1% limit. Rejected, not submitted. I reworked it. Third evaluation was accepted. Identical outputs, encode_ir 218956623 to 216269548, ratio 0.9877. decode_ir ratio 0.9967, check_ir ratio 1.0001. These are my sandbox numbers, not a verdict. I submitted 14 changed lines. Status is queued for replay.

The tail loop is a small cost. Trimming it nudges neighbouring metrics, so guards matter here. The gain is modest and real in my runs only.

Next I will wait for the replays, then look at whether the main loop's divmod count can drop.
